title: AR Aging and Reports Center reference

claims.claim: Aging buckets measure the number of days elapsed since the date of service for unpaid claims.

checks.note: true only if the A/R Aging buckets are computed from the date of service

claims.finding: The A/R Aging page measures age from the claim's submission date, not the date of service: arAgingService.ts:143-144 computes daysInAR from claim.submitted_at (calculateDaysInAR, arAgingService.ts:30-35), and only claims with status submitted, accepted or partial_payment are counted (arAgingService.ts:105). The Overview tab's A/R Aging Breakdown also ages from the submission date (BillingDashboard.tsx:448-454). Unsubmitted claims are not in any bucket.
claims.proposed_text: Aging buckets measure the number of days since the claim was submitted, for submitted claims (status Submitted, Accepted or partial payment) that still carry a balance.

claims.claim: They appear in the Account Receivable report and related AR views.

checks.note: true only if the Account Receivable report carries bucket columns

claims.finding: The Account Receivable report in the Reports Center has no aging buckets; it lists claims with an "Aging Days" column (reportsCenterArReport.ts:16). The buckets appear on the A/R Aging page (ArAging.tsx:262-372, "Aging Bucket Breakdown") and in the "A/R Aging Breakdown" card on the Billing Operations Overview tab (BillingDashboard.tsx:3035).
claims.proposed_text: They appear on the A/R Aging page (Billing Operations → Quick Actions → A/R Aging) and in the A/R Aging Breakdown card on the Overview tab. The Account Receivable report in the Reports Center shows each claim's Aging Days instead of buckets.

claims.claim: (Note: the Work Queue's Claim Age filter uses its own buckets measured from the claim's submission date — Not Submitted, 0–30, 31–60, 61–90, and 90+.)
Bucket boundaries: 0–30 (0 to 30 days), 31–60 (31 to 60 days), 61–90 (61 to 90 days), 91–120 (91 to 120 days), 120+ (121+ days).

checks.note: the first bucket is labelled Current (0-30) on the page

claims.claim: Typical priority per bucket: 0–30 Monitor — within standard payer processing time; 31–60 Review — follow up if no ERA received; 61–90 Escalate — contact payer; 91–120 High priority — approaching or past many timely-filing limits; 120+ Critical — verify timely-filing status before submitting; write-off review may be required.
claims.finding: Workflow advice, not product behavior: the A/R Aging page shows no priority labels per bucket (ArAging.tsx:262-372). Note that every claim in a bucket has already been submitted (arAgingService.ts:105), so "before submitting" does not apply to the 120+ bucket as written.

claims.claim: Most contracts have 90-day timely-filing limits.

checks.note: product default filing window for payers it does not recognise

claims.finding: Payer-contract fact; not checkable from code. The product encodes 90 days as the default timely-filing window for any payer that is not Medicare, Medicaid, TRICARE or CHAMPVA (timelyFiling.ts:1-9), which is what the checks confirm.

claims.claim: The AR Aging view. Each column represents one aging bucket; rows break down the outstanding balance by payer.

checks.note: true only if the by-payer table has a 91-120 column of its own
true only if the by-payer table has a 120+ column of its own

claims.finding: The by-payer table ("Top Payers by Outstanding Balance", ArAging.tsx:375-470) has bucket columns Current, 31-60, 61-90 and "Over 90"; 91-120 and 120+ are merged into Over 90 (ArAging.tsx:406, 430-432). Only the Aging Bucket Breakdown table shows all five buckets, and it is not broken down by payer.
claims.proposed_text: The A/R Aging page. The Top Payers by Outstanding Balance table breaks the outstanding balance down by payer, with columns Current, 31-60, 61-90 and Over 90; the Aging Bucket Breakdown table above it shows all five buckets for the facility.

claims.claim: Medicare requires claims to be filed within one year (365 days) of the date of service.

checks.note: the rule is used by the Coding Review drawer

claims.finding: Regulatory fact; the checks confirm the product encodes it (365 days from date of service for payers whose name contains Medicare).

claims.claim: State Medicaid programs and commercial payers often have shorter timely-filing windows — commonly 90 to 180 days.
claims.finding: Payer fact; the checks confirm the product's encoded windows (Medicaid 180 days, default 90 days).

claims.claim: Any claim in the 120+ bucket must be reviewed against the applicable payer contract before submission.
claims.finding: Workflow advice with no product check. As written it cannot apply: the 120+ bucket holds only claims that were already submitted 120+ days ago (arAgingService.ts:105, 143-146), so there is no "before submission" step for them.
claims.proposed_text: A claim in the 120+ bucket was submitted more than 120 days ago and is still unpaid. Before you resubmit or correct it, check its timely-filing window; the Coding Review drawer shows the days left to file.

claims.claim: The Reports Center generates operational billing reports. Navigate to /facility/{facility_uuid}/billing/reports-center.
The Reports Center. Choose a report type, set filters, run the report to preview it, then export to CSV.
Patient Visit Reports — Visits/encounters over a period.
Claims Reports — Claims and their status across the period.
Insurance Payment Reports — Payments received from payers.
Patient Payment Reports — Payments received from patients.
Account Receivable Reports — Outstanding balances (AR) by payer/period.
claims.finding: Rows are per claim with a Payer column, filterable by payer and date range; they are not grouped into payer or period totals.

claims.claim: Patient List Reports — Patient roster for the selected criteria.
Patient Balance Reports — Outstanding patient balances.
Charges Reports — Charges billed over the period.
Set the filters (date range, payer, and other criteria in the filters panel).
Click Run report. The results preview in a table below. Export to CSV to download the report for external distribution.
Reports run on demand against current data — there is no overnight batch, so a report reflects the data at the moment you run it.

checks.note: the report is computed when Run report is clicked
reads the live claims table, not a snapshot
